7. Workmanship

and Finish good diamond

7.1 Diamond shall be sintered into a steel shank in a suitable metal matrix having holding properties at a temperature below 750�C to prevent oxidation of diamond,

7.2 Brazing of diamond to the steel shank is not permitted as diamond will crack/oxidize All diamond points shall be natural and bruting of points is not permitted. temperatures. 8. Marking 8.1 Each tool shall a) Nominal b) Nominal c) Diamond be marked with the following information:

at high

name or trade-mark. Marking Details available with the Indian Standards Institution.

and Packing

9.1 The diamond truing/dressing tools shall be packed securely in suitable containers with suitable cushioning material to prevent movement of each tool within the containers and adequately cased, so that the tool is capable of withstanding normal transit risks. The diamond portion of the tool shall be suitably protected.

Correct wheel balance; Rigidity of mounting; Angle of presentation - The diamond shall be presented to the wheel in a trailing attitude. The angle between the axis of the truing tool holder and a line drawn through the centre of the grinding wheel and the point of contact in the periphery shall be 5" and 15" (see Fig. 5 ); Cutting edge -The cutting edge of the diamond shall be on the centre line of the grinding wheel at the point of contact; Depth of cut - The depth of cut in general shall not exceed 0.05 mm; Adequacy of coo/ant system, where used - It is essential that the coolant shall be turned on In case the diamond is accidently overbefore the diamond makes contact with the wheel. heated, it shall not be quenched, as this may cause the diamond to shatter. A-4.1 For diamond truing tools with morse/metric taper, tapered tool holder is the most suitable The tool when fitted in this holder does not get loosened by vibration and remains stable. EXPLANATORY

NOTE

This standard was first published by the Small Tools Sectional Committee, EDC 45, in 1964, in response to the request from manufacturers and users for providing a uniform system of processing diamond truing tools. This standard was later on transferred to the Abrasives Sectional Committee as it related to the work looked after by it. This standard is being revised so as to bring it in line In this revision the following additions have with the various practices followed in the industry. been made: a) Truing b) Material; c) The diamond grade and the permissible variation metric in the weight carat weight of diamond; and required for a tools with metric taper shank:

d) The method of finding out the correct particular grinding wheel.

of the diamond

Truing/dressing tools which have a diamond tip are used for truing/dressing the grinding wheel when the grinding surface has been worn out. The diamond truing tools may have a single diamond or several diamonds set in a suitable pattern which may be presented to the grinding wheel for dressing it. In this standard only the truing tools having a single diamond have been covered. ln the preparation of this standard, considerable 1973 ` Dimensions for Diamond Truing Tools ' issued 8
